analysis: Examined head lines 916-1718 of ClusterOnboardingLive.swift (model list planning, presentedChoices, provisioning, adopt, register, serve, settleTest, localServe). The visible security-relevant changes are a stop-since counter (stopsAsked / serve(unlessStoppedSince:) / localServe guarded by ClusterOnboardingStopped.asked) and a followerStatus that adds stopsAsked to status replies. These are fail-safe: a stop requested during a start keeps the pair stopped, and localServe returns .stopped before any serve is issued. The counter travels over the paired, authenticated cluster link (ClusterSetupLinkExchange.command with pairing), so I see no new trust-boundary exposure. Residual checks: the `command()` function still fills claim and the local token as before; `request.stopsBefore` is a peer-supplied integer, and a malicious paired peer could at worst cause its own stop to be honored or not, which the paired peer can already do. Model-copy trust (ClusterModelCopyTrust.servableArtifacts, approved() and the manifest-digest verification on copy/download) is unchanged in the visible context; presentedChoices only relabels blockers and cannot make an unservable model servable, since offers still require servableArtifacts membership. The privateImageQualification path suppresses peer copies and labels public traffic as prohibited, which is conservative. The patch excerpt is truncated, so the later hunks (around base 2217-2563, head 2238-2597) and the definitions of stopsAsked, ClusterOnboardingStopped and the request/reply struct fields are not visible here; I could not verify that the stop counter is monotonic across restarts or persisted correctly, nor the peer-side handling of stopsBefore. These concern availability (T-059/T-060-style) only, with no confirmed regression. The provider-to-coordinator, attestation and prefix-cache boundaries are not touched by the visible lines.
